lesson_title: The Better Buy: Why the Bigger Box Won
hook_text: 6 eggs for R21 or 18 eggs for R54? Most people pick wrong. Here is the 10-second fix.
clip_script: The most useful rate is the rate for ONE — the unit rate. Here is why. Shop A sells six eggs for R21. Shop B sells eighteen eggs for R54. Which is the better buy? You cannot compare R21 with R54 directly, because the boxes are different sizes. So bring both down to one egg. Shop A: R21 divided by six is R3,50 an egg. Shop B: R54 divided by eighteen is R3 an egg. Shop B is cheaper, even though its box costs more. Price per one is the only fair comparison, and the shops know most people will not do it.
visual_style: Two egg boxes side by side with price tags; each box splits into single eggs that line up under their price, and a per-egg tag drops onto one egg from each line — R3,50 in red, R3 in green.
pacing: Quick setup, a beat on the two boxes, then the two divisions land one after the other.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to share, scale and compare like a pro.
